title: FD Details in Consolidated Account Statement: What it Means for Investors
description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is set to integrate Fixed Deposit (FD) details into the Consolidated Account Statement (CAS). This initiative aims to provide .

faq.q: What is a Consolidated Account Statement (CAS)?
faq.a: A Consolidated Account Statement (CAS) is a single statement issued by depositories (NSDL/CDSL) that provides a comprehensive view of an investor's holdings in demat accounts (shares, bonds) and mutual funds under one PAN.

faq.q: Which FDs will be included in the CAS?
faq.a: The RBI's initiative aims to include details of Fixed Deposits (FDs) held with banks. This will likely cover FDs linked to your Permanent Account Number (PAN) across various commercial and potentially co-operative banks.

faq.q: When can I expect to see my FD details in CAS?
faq.a: The implementation of this enhanced CAS, including FD details, is expected to be completed by December 31, 2026.

faq.q: Will this impact my tax filing?
faq.a: While the CAS itself is an information statement, its enhanced details, including FDs, will make it significantly easier for you to track your total interest income. This can simplify the process of accurately reporting income and complying with income tax regulations during ITR filing.
The Consolidated Account Statement (CAS) is issued by depositories, namely National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL) and Central Depository Services (India) Limited (CDSL).

faq.q: Can I opt out of this feature?
faq.a: The integration of FD details into the CAS is a regulatory initiative by the RBI, aimed at enhancing transparency and ease of financial tracking. It is generally expected to be a standard feature for all investors, similar to how mutual fund and demat holdings are currently included.

faq.q: Will my joint FDs also be included?
faq.a: Details regarding joint FDs and how they will be presented in the CAS are yet to be fully clarified. However, typically, statements are linked to the primary PAN holder. It is expected that systems will evolve to handle joint holdings appropriately.
